description: Moth swarm — 20k agents, positive phototaxis, spiral orbit around lamp, fatigue-driven inward decay (Miller's spiral).
reference: Hsiao 1972 — Positive phototaxis and the Miller's Spiral; Baker & Woiwod 1979
notes: Moths use a fixed-angle flight relative to the moon for navigation (transverse orientation). Artificial lamps confuse this: the moth spirals inward (Miller's spiral) as it tries to maintain a constant angle to a near-field source, eventually hitting the lamp or exhausting itself.
